one_line_contribution: That cross-model agent-memory harm is not symmetric identity mismatch but a *signed* writer→reader capability effect, that the fix is reader-in-the-loop selection rather than reader authorship (shown in both the memory and instruction slots), and that coupling a GEPA-style optimizer to a memory bank masks the residual harm at the net-accuracy level while the break asymmetry survives underneath.
closest_prior_work: Rosetta Memory (arXiv:2606.07711) and AMD (arXiv:2608.07169). AMD already reports that teacher→student memory transfer 'yields inconsistent improvements and in several cases degrades performance' and that quality depends on 'teacher–student compatibility' — so both the harm and a compatibility term are prior, and the proposal concedes this. Rosetta threatens the framing, and the proposal's escape hatch is weaker than it claims: it asserts that identity/style accounts are 'symmetric' and therefore falsified by run D. That is a straw version of the rival. A style/brittleness account predicts asymmetry too, because a weaker reader is more perturbable by *any* off-distribution phrasing than a stronger one is; harm falling harder on the 8B is exactly what Rosetta's mechanism would produce without any ordinal capability law. So the single cell that is supposed to separate this proposal from its closest competitor does not separate them.
strongest_objection: The two headline claims rest on cells that are both underpowered and, by the proposal's own accounting, non-primary. (a) Run D — the direction-asymmetry cell, explicitly billed as 'the discriminating test' against Rosetta/MemCollab — is 2 runs with a single bank replicate, and Measurement §(b) says non-primary single-replicate cells are 'reported as directional only'. Its DiD MDE is ~6 points and prediction 1 asks for exactly ≥6: any positive is at the detection edge, and the mirror leg is stated as 'no penalty of comparable size', i.e. accepting a null in the cell with the *largest* variance in the design. The proposal itself refuses to read a sub-6 null as parity for run L; prediction 1 does precisely that for run D. (b) Prediction 5, the masking result, is defined as H−I 'falling below the MDE' — again a null, again in single-replicate cells (H and I are 2 runs each, one per reader), against a noise floor the proposal admits produced 5–14 point drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment. A shrinking net delta under GEPA is equally explained by GEPA raising accuracy toward ceiling, by GEPA reducing discordant-pair rate (and hence power), or by the single replicate. As written, the most novel claim in the paper is an underpowered null dressed as a mechanism.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Reallocate bank replicates: run D and the H/I masking pair need two replicates each, more than run E or L do. 2) Replace every 'falls below the MDE' with a preregistered equivalence test (TOST) against a stated equivalence margin, and report the GEPA-condition discordant-pair rate so a power loss cannot be sold as masking. 3) Add a mismatch-without-capability-gap arm: have the frontier rewrite the 8B's *own* items in frontier style/abstraction without adding content, and read it with the 8B. If that arm harms as much as the frontier-authored bank, the effect is style brittleness and the signed-gap law is dead — run E (frontier writing from 8B traces) is the closest thing to this but is a single unreplicated run with no prediction attached to it, so it currently carries no inferential weight. 4) Fix the replicate construction: splitting the 150–250-item intersection into disjoint halves means the primary contrasts are run on 75–125-item banks, so retrieval hit-rate differs from the precheck and from run F; use bootstrap or overlapping resamples at full bank size, or report bank size as a covariate. 5) State what the token 'padding' in runs C and K actually contains — padding is itself a treatment that may differentially load the small reader's context, and it is doing load-bearing work in the one arm (K) that supports the selection claim.
missing_baseline: A quality-agnostic subsetting control for run K. The track's own established result is that injection *volume* is the causal lever (7 items → 3 items eliminated the harm from the identical bank). Reader-probe admission removes items; padding restores tokens but not distinct advice. So K vs C confounds 'reader selected' with 'fewer distinct items', and prediction 4(a) can be satisfied by volume alone. Required: (i) random-subset frontier bank matched to K's retained item count, (ii) judge-quality-top-k frontier bank at the same count (selection by a non-reader criterion), and (iii) probe selection performed with the *other* reader's probes — only (iii) shows selection must be reader-specific rather than merely a filter. The same hole exists in the instruction slot: G vs J is not 'same author, selection is the only difference' — GEPA also gets 12 candidates and iterative reflection on rollout traces, while J is one cold instruction. The demanded control is frontier-authored best-of-12 selected by the frontier (or by the other reader's rollouts), not a single cold write.
preprint_collision: Among the better collision checks I have seen on the memory side: it names three colliding 2026 preprints with IDs, quotes AMD against its own interest, concedes that 'cross-model agent memory transfers badly' is no longer novel, dispositions five further papers, and states a residual risk. I credit it and it materially raises my confidence in the positioning. Two gaps keep it from being clean. First, it searched only the memory literature. The most novel claim in the proposal — that a prompt optimizer absorbs and hides a coupled component's harm — has no search behind it at all: no query for GEPA/MIPRO + memory coupling, component attribution, or optimizer-masking preprints, and the cited Cross-Component Interference paper (2605.05716) is the obvious neighbourhood where a masking result could already sit. Second, 'No matching OpenReview submission was found' names no venue, cycle, or date, and given three concurrent cross-model memory preprints it is quite likely that at least one already runs both transfer directions in an evaluation matrix without calling it signed — which would reduce the asymmetry claim from a new law to a reframing of an existing table. The proposal anticipates this only for a 'self-written-bank ablation in an appendix'.
